The Montgomery County Circuit Court was established in 1776 when Maryland was still a British colony. It is one of the oldest courts in the state of Maryland. The current courthouse was built in 1931 and has since undergone several renovations and expansions.

Procedures in the Montgomery County Circuit Court

Filing a Case

To file a case in the Montgomery County Circuit Court, the plaintiff must submit a complaint to the court. The complaint must include information about the plaintiff, the defendant, and the nature of the case. The plaintiff must also pay a filing fee, which varies depending on the type of case.

Pretrial Conference

After the case has been filed, the court will schedule a pretrial conference. The pretrial conference is an opportunity for both parties to discuss the case and attempt to reach a settlement. If a settlement is not reached, the case will proceed to trial.

Discovery Process

During the discovery process, both parties are required to exchange information relevant to the case. This can include documents, witness statements, and other evidence. The goal of the discovery process is to ensure that both parties have access to all the necessary information before the trial.

Trial

The trial is the final stage of the court proceedings. During the trial, both parties present their case before a judge or a jury. The judge or the jury will then decide on the outcome of the case. If the case involves a jury, the jury will deliberate and reach a verdict.
